 Here is today’s weather by province: Mpumalanga swings from cool morning to stormy hot afternoon
 Kimberley and Mahikeng share the top spot at 35°C, Polokwane enjoys the only clear skies, and SAWS has no active warnings in place.
 By
 Thandi Mokoena 
 26-10-26 06:00 
 in
 Weather 
 0 
 Today's weather across the nine provinces, with the moon phase. Visuals by PubgentIQ AI 
 Across much of South Africa, Monday brings a warm, unsettled day. Showers and thundershowers are expected across the interior, including Bloemfontein, Kimberley, Mahikeng and Mbombela, and Durban gets the same with a mild 20°C to 22°C. Johannesburg stays partly cloudy and pleasant, peaking at 29°C. Down south, Cape Town sits under cloud with a brisk SSE wind, and Gqeberha can expect rain showers.
 Kimberley and Mahikeng share the top spot at 35°C, while Polokwane enjoys the only clear skies at 32°C. Mbombela has the chilliest start at 14°C. Coastal Cape Town is the coolest by afternoon, reaching just 21°C. Happily, SAWS has no active warnings in place.
 Warnings and Advisories
 Advice Impact-Based Warnings: Yellow Level 2 Warning: Severe thunderstorms with heavy downpours, damaging winds, hail and lightning resulting in localised flooding and damage to infrastructure and settlements are expected over most parts of KwaZulu-Natal except in the extreme north-east, as well as the extreme northern parts of Eastern Cape.
 Advice Fire Danger Warnings: Extremely high fire danger conditions are expected over the North-West, central and eastern Northern Cape, most parts of both Free State and Limpopo as well as in places in both western KwaZulu-Natal and western parts of the Northern Cape.
 Advice Advisories: Hot and humid conditions will result in extremely uncomfortable conditions in the north-eastern parts of KwaZulu Natal on Monday.
